risksForTheArchitect: R1 — a reusable reading fault, and the one worth passing on from this round. `gh run list --commit <sha>` returns an empty list for a short SHA and the full list for the same commit's 40-character SHA: at the merge head, `--commit 4cbc967e4232` printed nothing while `--commit 4cbc967e4232c2e75a76bd2bdb80423398bb7603` printed six runs, in the same second. That is the false negative I met at cc604381a4bd last round and reported then as 'gh run list is unreliable here'; the cause is the argument, not the command. The REST check-runs endpoint accepts the short form and is the better second source. Worth the fleet note, since a short SHA is what a log line or a jj template hands you.

R2 — main has moved one commit past the merge again since this merge landed (`decf80f922a1 feat(daemon): wake a production check at each deploy workflow run (#2203)`, GitHub `behind_by 1`), and it does not conflict: mergeable is true.
